## What I implemented

- `connectors/src/connectors/errors.py`
  - `RegistryError(Exception)` base class.
  - `UnknownConnectorKindError(RegistryError)`: `__init__(self, name: str)` stores `self.name` and
    message `unknown connector kind '<name>'; known kinds: mcp`.
  - `DuplicateConnectorError(RegistryError)`, `ConnectorNotFoundError(RegistryError)`.
  - `KNOWN_CONNECTOR_KINDS = ("mcp",)` constant for the message.
- `connectors/src/connectors/models.py` (Pydantic `BaseModel`s)
  - `HealthStatus(ok: bool, detail: str = "")`
  - `McpConnectorSettings(url: str, tools: list[str] = [])`
  - `ConnectorConfig(name, kind="mcp", enabled=True, settings={})` with
    `mcp_settings()` dispatching on `self.kind`; raises
    `UnknownConnectorKindError(name=self.kind)` when `kind != "mcp"`, otherwise
    `McpConnectorSettings.model_validate(self.settings)`.
  - `IngestRecord(id, source_name, source_kind, item_type: Literal["resource","tool_result","catalog"], name, content, raw={})`
  - `IngestBatch(connector_name, records=[], errors=[])`
  - Mutable defaults use `Field(default_factory=...)` (Pydantic-safe equivalent of the brief's `= []`/`= {}`).
- `connectors/src/connectors/protocol.py`
  - `@runtime_checkable Connector(Protocol)` with `kind: str`, `name: str`,
    `async def health() -> HealthStatus`, `async def ingest() -> IngestBatch`.
- `connectors/src/connectors/__init__.py`
  - Re-exports models, `Connector`, and all four error classes; declares `__all__`.
- `connectors/tests/test_models.py` — the brief's test, copied verbatim.
